summary: This is an April 1st joke RFC proposing a new ICMP message that a router or host could use to tell a host to slow down when it ignores other signals like packet loss and ECN. It is humorous and not for real use.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7514 is an April 1st joke proposing a message that literally tells a host to slow down when it ignores congestion signals. The message carries a short text notification for the user.

subtitle: An April 1st joke proposing an ICMP message that tells senders to slow down.

tldr.problem: This April 1st joke imagines senders that ignore packet loss and ECN congestion signals.
tldr.mechanism: It proposes an ICMP RECN message with a four-byte ASCII notification that a host presents to the user.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7514 is an Experimental joke RFC; it assigns no IANA values at publication and describes a two-year experiment.

today: RFC 7514 is Experimental and dated April 1, 2015. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The RECN Proposal
sections.content: RFC 7514 is an April 1st joke that proposes Really Explicit Congestion Notification (RECN). It imagines a router or host advising a sender to reduce its sending rate when the sender has not reacted to packet loss or Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN). The RFC describes this as a less subtle signal.
sections.plainLanguage: This April 1st joke gives the network a more direct way to tell a sender to slow down. It is aimed at a host that has ignored packet loss and ECN.

sections.title: Message Contents and Presentation
sections.content: The proposed ICMP message contains a four-byte Explicit Notification field in ASCII. The RFC says the contents MUST be conveyed to the user responsible for the traffic. If text-to-speech is available, the text should be spoken; if the system is muted, a pop-up message will suffice. The RFC also describes routers sending messages for packets discarded in a burst.
sections.plainLanguage: The message contains four bytes of text. The RFC says the host should present it to the user, by speech or a pop-up.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC notes that forged ICMP messages could cause a host to reduce its sending rate without cause. It says a host must check that the quoted packet belongs to an active flow. For IPv4, the RFC also includes a requirement involving the security flag defined in RFC 3514.
sections.plainLanguage: A forged message could falsely tell a host to slow down. The RFC says the host should check that the message refers to an active flow.
